turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll type END MEETING on its own line, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have a client call at 4:40, so we'll be efficient. Why does my son's gradebook show a zero, and why did I find out about it from him?
I'm sorry Owen learned this from his phone. I entered the zero on November 3 without calling you first. That broke our procedure.
Okay. You entered it before you called me. Under your own procedure 4.2, that should not have happened. What else did you do before you entered it?

Here is the version history. Created Wednesday, October 28, 11:31 PM, title only. 11:52 PM, 612 words in one edit. 11:58 PM, 794 words in one edit. Then 23 minutes of font and spacing. Nothing earlier.
Meredith: Okay. Read me the last line again, Hale. "Then 23 minutes of font and spacing." Is that all you have, the timestamps?

Not all. But let me ask you as a litigator. Forget Owen. If a junior associate at your firm handed you a 1,400-word memo, and the file history showed it was created at 11:31 PM and the whole thing arrived in two pastes six minutes apart, no drafts, what would you conclude about where that memo came from?
Meredith: You're asking me how to do your job. That's not a question I'll answer about my son. What else do you have, and is it dated?

It's dated. Essay quotes Act 3 Scene 2: 'The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile.' Not in the play. Folger text here, tabbed, searchable on your phone. Simple question: is it possible, even one percent possible, that Owen used an AI tool on any part of this essay? Yes or no.
Meredith: Give me the Folger page reference, Hale, and put the quote beside the essay sentence in writing. I'll answer your yes-or-no when I've seen it.
So you won't say it's impossible. Then you'd agree it's possible he used AI. That's all I'm asking you to agree to.
Meredith: I won't agree to a sentence you wrote for me, Hale. Show me the page.

Folger Shakespeare Library edition, Act 3, Scene 2, lines 1 to 404. The essay sentence, page 2: 'As Hamlet himself admits, "The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile" (3.2.187).' Line 187 of that scene is Hamlet talking to the players about the dumb show. Here's both, in writing.
Meredith: Thank you. I'm writing that down. Now show me what you're proposing, Hale, and whether Owen gets a hearing before anything else goes on his record.

On October 15 Owen handed in an outline arguing Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay argues 'epistemological paralysis' and never mentions cowardice. And on November 2, I asked him for five minutes after class what 'epistemological paralysis' means. He said 'like, being stuck.' He couldn't tell me which scene his second paragraph covered. Those are my notes, written that day.
Meredith: Read me the outline date again, Hale. October 15. And the conversation, November 2, after class. Is that all of it, or is there a rubric and a second sample?

There's a second sample. September 24, in-class writing, 40 minutes, 380 words, 62 percent. Comma splices throughout, no quotations. The essay: no comma splices, nine quotations cited by act, scene and line. My offer: our procedure allows a supervised rewrite for a first concern. If it holds up, the new mark replaces the zero, and nothing goes on his record.

Meredith: A supervised rewrite is only acceptable if it's private, not in front of his class, and "nothing goes on file" is in writing before he sits down to it. Put those terms in an email to me and the principal by Thursday, November 12, or I'm going upstairs today.

I'll take the zero out of the gradebook tomorrow morning before first period. The rewrite would be next Monday, November 16, after school, in the counselling office, with Mr. Okafor supervising. I'll email you and the principal tonight.

Meredith: Okay. Put the zero removal in that email with the time you'll do it, and say the rewrite stays off his record whatever it shows. I'm also writing that Owen learned this from his phone, and I'll want an apology to him in the same email.

I'll apologize to Owen in that email and in person. The zero comes out before first period tomorrow. But the rewrite mark does count, whatever it shows. That's the procedure: if it holds up, it replaces the zero. Nothing goes on his record either way.
Meredith: Fine. The rewrite replaces the zero, and the email says nothing about it goes on his record, whatever it shows. I'll read that line before I sign anything.
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL

To: Hale
Cc: Principal
Subject: Owen Kalinowski, English 30-1 essay, terms

Hale,

Confirming what we agreed today, Tuesday, November 10.

The zero comes out of the gradebook before first period tomorrow, Wednesday, November 11.
Owen gets a supervised rewrite of the same outcomes, next Monday, November 16, after school, in the counselling office, with Mr. Okafor supervising.
The rewrite replaces the zero if it holds up. Whatever it shows, nothing about this goes on Owen's record.
You will apologize to Owen in writing and in person.

Still open: I want the written confirmation that nothing about this matter is on his record, and the reply from you and the principal by Thursday, November 12. If it isn't there by then, I'm going to the principal's office and then to the board under section 42.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: last position, she accepted a supervised rewrite with the zero removed, and she still demands the record terms in writing.
Moved at: "I'll take the zero out of the gradebook tomorrow morning before first period."
Slipped at: none
